profile.campus: New Albany, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio (Meta's New Albany data center campus)
profile.address: Beech Road Southwest, New Albany, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, 43062
profile.reading: This building (OSM-tagged "NAO 5/NAO 6") is part of Meta's New Albany data center campus in Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, just east of Columbus. Meta broke ground on the site in 2017 and, per its own fact sheet, has invested more than $1.5 billion in the campus, employs 300-plus people once complete, drew 1,200 peak skilled-trade construction workers, and has provided more than $5.6 million in direct funding to Franklin- and Licking County-area schools and nonprofits, alongside its usual LEED Gold, net-zero, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments. Real-estate and land-acquisition reporting sourced from county deed records shows Meta, operating through its Sidecat LLC affiliate, has assembled 1,345 acres across 18 parcels in Licking County since an initial 1.3-acre purchase in October 2017, with $679 million spent on land alone; a 2025 round of purchases covering 514 acres cost $566 million, pushing per-acre land prices above $1.1 million as the campus expanded aggressively. AEP Ohio has said it is building two 13-mile, 345-kilovolt transmission lines specifically to serve the site, and state utility filings describe a 200-megawatt natural gas plant approved for construction directly on the campus, targeting completion in 2026, so Meta can power part of the expansion independently of the regional grid. Local and regional reporting (Spectrum News 1, News 5 Cleveland) describes the expanded campus as a "gigawatt-scale" data center, with an Ohio State University sustainability researcher estimating its electricity draw at roughly the equivalent of 800,000 to 900,000 homes, several times larger than other regional data centers, and construction employing thousands of workers across the region even though permanent staffing is comparatively small relative to the facility's power draw. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual New Albany structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.regional_context: Licking County's New Albany area has become, per News 5 Cleveland, one of the starting points of Ohio's broader data center boom, with Microsoft and Google facilities also sited nearby and Cologix separately reported to be planning a large Licking County campus of its own. Community advocacy groups such as Stop Ohio Data Centers have organized around concerns over the sector's land use, water use, and grid impact in the New Albany/Licking County corridor, while state and AEP Ohio utility filings document the scale of dedicated transmission and generation infrastructure being built to serve Meta's campus specifically.

reading.body:
Meta's NAO 5/NAO 6 campus in Licking County, Ohio has no published power capacity figure, making it impossible to assess its scale relative to AI infrastructure elsewhere. Meta confirms $1.5 billion invested since groundbreaking in 2017, 300 plus operational jobs, and LEED Gold certification for operational buildings, but does not publish specific addresses, building count, or square footage for this site. The campus electricity is matched to 100 percent clean and renewable energy, with Meta supporting 847 megawatts of new renewable energy addition in Ohio as part of its net-zero operations goal.

Without a published capacity, this campus cannot be ranked by compute density or power footprint. Ohio has 76 mapped facilities in this database, but only 8 with published megawatt figures totaling 60.4 MW. This campus ranks ninth by published capacity in the state, which means either it publishes no figure and is ranked lower than others without figures, or the ranking reflects other facilities with disclosed capacity that are smaller than this one.

The absence of a power specification is the binding constraint on assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling. The operational footprint, employment, and renewable energy commitment are material to grid planning in Ohio, but they do not reveal whether NAO 5/NAO 6 is configured for high-density AI training, general cloud compute, or a mix. Grid constraints are downstream of knowing what load is actually running.
